title: A year that measures distance: the light-year

sources.title: What Is a Light-Year? (NASA Space Place)

publish.title: A year that measures distance: the light-year
publish.description: What a light-year is, and how far away the nearest star is.

scenes.headline: A year is a distance?
scenes.narration: A light-year sounds like time. It is actually a distance, and a huge one.

scenes.headline: What a light-year is
scenes.narration: A light-year is how far light travels in one year.

definition.meaning: The distance light travels in one year, about 9.46 trillion kilometres.

scenes.headline: The number
scenes.narration: That is about nine point four six trillion kilometres.

scenes.headline: The nearest star
scenes.narration: The nearest star beyond our Sun, Proxima Centauri, is about four point two light-years away.

scenes.headline: Looking back in time
scenes.narration: Light takes time to arrive, so you see distant objects as they were. Light from Proxima left about four years ago.

scenes.headline: Look up tonight
scenes.narration: Every point of light you see left its star long ago.
